questions.enonce_markdown:
Prove that the circles $S_1$ and $S_2$, where
$$
S_1:\ x^2 + y^2 + 2x - 8y + 8 = 0,
$$
$$
S_2:\ x^2 + y^2 + 10x - 2y + 22 = 0,
$$
touch each other externally and find the equation of the common tangent at the point of contact. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Centres and radii.** Complete the squares.

$S_1$: $(x + 1)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 1 + 16 - 8 = 9$, so centre $C_1(-1, 4)$ and radius $r_1 = 3$.

$S_2$: $(x + 5)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 25 + 1 - 22 = 4$, so centre $C_2(-5, 1)$ and radius $r_2 = 2$.

**External contact.** The distance between the centres is
$$
C_1C_2 = \sqrt{(-5 + 1)^2 + (1 - 4)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5 = 3 + 2 = r_1 + r_2.
$$
The distance between the centres equals the sum of the radii, so the circles touch each other externally (at exactly one point). $\blacksquare$

**Point of contact.** It lies on the segment $C_1C_2$, at distance $3$ from $C_1$, i.e. at the fraction $\dfrac35$ of the way from $C_1$ to $C_2$:
$$
P = \left(-1 + \tfrac35(-4),\ 4 + \tfrac35(-3)\right) = \left(-\tfrac{17}{5},\ \tfrac{11}{5}\right).
$$
(Check on $S_1$: $\left(-\frac{17}{5} + 1\right)^2 + \left(\frac{11}{5} - 4\right)^2 = \frac{144}{25} + \frac{81}{25} = 9$; on $S_2$: $\left(-\frac{17}{5} + 5\right)^2 + \left(\frac{11}{5} - 1\right)^2 = \frac{64}{25} + \frac{36}{25} = 4$.)

**Common tangent.** The tangent at $P$ is perpendicular to the line of centres. The gradient of $C_1C_2$ is $\dfrac{1 - 4}{-5 + 1} = \dfrac34$, so the tangent has gradient $-\dfrac43$:
$$
y - \frac{11}{5} = -\frac43\left(x + \frac{17}{5}\right)
\;\Rightarrow\;
15y - 33 = -20x - 68
\;\Rightarrow\;
20x + 15y + 35 = 0
\;\Rightarrow\;
4x + 3y + 7 = 0.
$$
(Second method: for touching circles, the common tangent at the point of contact is the radical axis $S_1 - S_2 = 0$: $(2x - 8y + 8) - (10x - 2y + 22) = -8x - 6y - 14 = 0$, i.e. $4x + 3y + 7 = 0$. It passes through $P$: $4\left(-\frac{17}{5}\right) + 3\cdot\frac{11}{5} + 7 = \frac{-68 + 33 + 35}{5} = 0$.)
$$\boxed{\text{Common tangent: } 4x + 3y + 7 = 0 \quad \text{at the point of contact } \left(-\tfrac{17}{5},\ \tfrac{11}{5}\right)}$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
Two statements are denoted by $p$ and $q$. Construct the truth table for the compound statement $m$, where
$$
m = (p \wedge q) \vee (\sim q).
$$
(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
List the four possible combinations of truth values of $p$ and $q$, then evaluate $p \wedge q$ (true only when both are true), $\sim q$ (negation of $q$) and finally the disjunction $m$ (true when at least one of $p \wedge q$, $\sim q$ is true).

| $p$ | $q$ | $p \wedge q$ | $\sim q$ | $m = (p \wedge q) \vee (\sim q)$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | T | F | **T** |
| T | F | F | T | **T** |
| F | T | F | F | **F** |
| F | F | F | T | **T** |

$m$ is false only when $p$ is false and $q$ is true. The last column is the same as that of $p \vee (\sim q)$, so $m \equiv p \vee (\sim q)$. The statement is neither a tautology nor a contradiction.
$$\boxed{m:\ \text{T, T, F, T}}$$
